To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PlGF and PlFG/VEGF heteromers are detected in the SF and synovial tissue of patients with inflammatory arthritis.
PlGF is present in the SF of inflammatory arthropathy and is a potent inducer of VEGF production by monocytes.
PlGF and PlG/VEGF hetero‐dimers are detected in SF and plasma from patients with a broad spectrum of inflammatory arthropathic conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of vascular permeability and angiogenesis in the inflammatory joint,
the role that PlGF may play in the pathophysiology of inflammatory arthritis.
the role of placenta growth factor (PIGF) in the pathophysiology of rheumatoid arthritis and other inflammatory arthropathic diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PlGF and PlGf‐VEGF heterodimiers are present in synovial fluids and plasma of patients suffering from a variety of inflammatory arthropathys.

PlGF, VEF, and PlGF/ VEGF heterodimers are present in synovial fluids of inflammatory joint disorders, that they correlate with the total and differential leucocyte counts, that PlGF upregulates the secretion of VEGF from peripheral blood mononucleated cells, that PlGF is present in plasma, and that VEGF is also present in plasma but not in the heterodimeric form.
PlGF and VEFGF heterodimers have an important role in inflammatory arthritis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PlGF and VEFG are detected in SF of inflammatory arthropathy, that PlGF is the most potent inducet of VEGF secretion and that PlGF/VEFg heterodimer levels are increased in RA.
PlGF, VEF and their heterodimers are present in the synovial fluid and blood of patients with a variety of inflammatory arthropathes.
PlGF is an important regulator of VEGF production, and that PlGF and Plgf/VEGF heterdimer levels in SF may reflect the degree of inflammation in arthritic joints.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PlGF may play a key role as a pro‐angiogenic factor in RA.
PlGF is a key player in the production of vascular endothelial growth factors (VEGFs) in the inflamed joint.
PlGF is present in the synovial fluid and plasma of patients, and it can be detected in the synovium by western blotting.
